speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent, and I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To understand your condition, please tell me: what is your exact age in days or hours, and how long has this difficulty breathing been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the baby was born at 33 weeks, are there any specific signs of chest wall retractions, grunting, or nasal flaring you have noticed? Also, what was the Apgar score at birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm newborn presenting with grunting, retractions, and cyanosis two hours after birth is classic for RDS due to surfactant deficiency; Tuberculosis is extremely unlikely in this acute neonatal timeframe and should be disregarded as an untrustled suggestion.
